**Plan.** The shape is a single closed rectangular cavity — no ports, no protrusions — so the OpenFOAM-native way to build it is `blockMesh`: one hex block, 0.1 × 0.06 × 0.04 m (I convert mm → m immediately, since OpenFOAM reads bare numbers as metres), all six faces in one patch called `walls`. The heater/cooler are *cell zones*, not geometry — the standard way is `topoSet` with `boxToCell`. I'll place the cubes on multiples of the 2 mm cell pitch so their boundaries land exactly on cell faces:

- `heater`: x ∈ [4, 24] mm, z ∈ [2, 22] mm (near floor, at the x=0 end)
- `cooler`: x ∈ [76, 96] mm, z ∈ [18, 38] mm (near ceiling, at the x=100 end)
- both centred across the width: y ∈ [20, 40] mm

Those placements (2 mm standoff from wall/end) are my choice — the request says only "near the floor/ceiling at one end". First cell: write the minimal case files and the blockMeshDict, mesh at 50×30×20 (30 k cells, 2 mm pitch), and run checkMesh.

Block mesh created cleanly: 30 000 hexahedra at 2 mm pitch, bounding box exactly (0 0 0)→(0.1 0.06 0.04), single `walls` patch. The checkMesh tail got cut off, but next cell reruns its verdict anyway.

Now the cell zones: `topoSet` with `boxToCell` for the two 20 mm cubes (placed on 2 mm multiples so zone boundaries coincide with cell faces), then `setsToZones` to turn them into cellZones.

Both zones came out at exactly 1000 cells = 10×10×10 cells = a 20 mm cube at 2 mm pitch, as designed. My checkMesh filter matched nothing, so let me print the actual verdict and confirm the zones landed in `constant/polyMesh/cellZones`, then look at the mesh.
The cellZones file exists in `constant/polyMesh`. The checkMesh output appears truncated right after "Create mesh" — let me get its full output and see whether it finished.
checkMesh in this build wants `divSchemes` present in fvSchemes. I'll fill in the standard default scheme subdictionaries and rerun.

`Mesh OK`, and every requested number checks out against the mesh itself:

- Domain: (0 0 0) → (0.1 0.06 0.04) m, total volume 2.4e-4 m³ = 100×60×40 mm ✓
- `heater` zone: 1000 cells, volume 8e-6 m³ = 20³ mm³, near the floor at x=0 end ✓
- `cooler` zone: 1000 cells, 8e-6 m³, near the ceiling at x=100 mm end ✓
- All 30000 cells hexahedra, aspect ratio 1, orthogonality 0, single closed `walls` patch ✓

Now a picture: export the mesh and the two zones to VTK and render them.
The render confirms it: the sealed box with the red `heater` cube low at the x = 0 end and the blue `cooler` cube high at the x = 100 mm end, both centred across the width.
